name: Mucinous cystic neoplasm of the pancreas

reference.source: Sleisenger and Fordtran's Gastrointestinal and Liver Disease
clinicalPearls: A mucin-producing cystic neoplasm that arises almost exclusively in women, typically in middle age
Characteristically located in the body or tail of the pancreas and, unlike IPMN, does not communicate with the pancreatic duct
Defined histologically by an ovarian-type stroma beneath the mucinous epithelium, a hallmark distinguishing it from other cystic lesions
Usually a single, large, thick-walled cyst that may contain septa and peripheral (eggshell) calcification
Considered a premalignant lesion with potential for progression to invasive mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
Cyst fluid typically shows a raised CEA reflecting its mucinous nature
Because of malignant potential and the generally younger, surgically fit population, resection is commonly recommended, particularly for larger or symptomatic lesions or those with worrisome features
reference.pathophysiology: Mucinous cystic neoplasms are thought to develop from primitive stroma, giving rise to the characteristic ovarian-type stroma that supports an overlying mucin-secreting columnar epithelium. This distinctive stroma expresses hormone receptors, in keeping with the striking female predominance. The lesions form solitary, septated cysts that, in contrast to intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, do not connect with the ductal system. The epithelium can progress through increasing grades of dysplasia to invasive cystadenocarcinoma, so the presence and extent of any invasive component determines behaviour; non-invasive lesions are cured by complete resection.
additionalDifferentials: Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm with cystic change
additionalInvestigations: MRI with MRCP to assess cyst morphology and confirm absence of ductal communication
Endoscopic ultrasound with fine-needle aspiration for fluid analysis and wall assessment
Cyst fluid CEA (typically elevated) and cytology
Cyst fluid molecular testing for KRAS mutation to support a mucinous diagnosis
Contrast-enhanced CT to detect mural nodules, solid components, and calcification
Serum CA 19-9 when malignancy is a concern
redFlags: An enhancing mural nodule or solid component within the cyst
Associated pancreatic duct dilatation or a discrete mass suggesting invasion
New symptoms such as pain, weight loss, or jaundice
reference.prognosis: Non-invasive mucinous cystic neoplasms are cured by complete surgical resection with an excellent long-term outlook; once invasive cystadenocarcinoma has developed, prognosis depends on stage and resembles that of pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
pitfalls: Confusing a mucinous cystic neoplasm with a benign serous cystadenoma or a pseudocyst
Assuming a body or tail cyst in a woman is benign without appropriate characterisation
Attributing the lesion to prior pancreatitis and mislabelling it a pseudocyst, delaying resection
Incomplete resection leaving residual neoplastic epithelium
Failing to appreciate that the absence of ductal communication helps separate it from IPMN
